rec.name: Collection Model View Toggle (Product vs. Model Images)
rec.status: Built — launched (code documented, support video available)

what.text: A toggle in the collection page's meta bar (next to the product count and sort-by) that switches all product-card images between the product-only shot and the on-model shot. It comes in three layouts: (1) a checkbox-style switch labelled e.g. 'Tragebilder' (worn images), (2) two text buttons 'Model | Product' with an underline on the active one, (3) a 'classic' layout with a title ('Opinion:') and two icons (a shirt for product-only, a person for model) with optional hover tooltips. The position in the meta bar can be left, center or right. It was implemented as a block inside the main-collection section, with a limit of 1 per section.

why.text: Shoppers in apparel and accessories want to see how an item looks when worn (fit, drape, scale) as well as the clean product shot for detail. Letting them choose their preferred view on the listing page reduces the need to open each PDP, speeds up browsing and comparison, and increases confidence and relevance. This gives the shopper control and improves product-card engagement and click-through. The toggle also stays visible without taking up product space, because it lives in the existing meta bar.

how.text: 1) In main-collection.liquid, replace the 'product-facet__meta-bar anchor' markup with the provided version, which renders the 'ed-model-view' snippet in the left, center or right slot depending on the setting. 2) Add a new schema block 'model_view' (limit 1) with settings for position, layout (checkbox/button/classic), the labels and the tooltip texts. 3) At the end of the section's top <style> tag, add the Liquid loop that reads the model_view block settings into variables (active_model_view, model_type, position, labels, tooltips). 4) Create the snippet ed-model-view.liquid containing the CSS, the markup for the three layouts and the JS. The JS toggles the class 'ed-ModelView-active' on the product list. The CSS then hides the first card image and shows the second one (and swaps them back on hover), so the theme must output the model image as the second image of each product card. In the theme editor, add the 'Model view' block to the collection page and set its options. Non-developers cannot install it, but once it is installed the block can be configured in the editor.

items: Classic layout: Tooltip text for product view and for model view

Ticket spec (original ask, not seen in the code): visibility on/off, design variation, background color, text color, icon and toggle colors (active/inactive). The delivered code only exposes the settings listed above; the toggle colors are hard-coded (#e6e6e6 inactive, black knob when active).

dependencies.text: Needs a Shopify theme whose collection section is main-collection.liquid, with the classes 'product-facet__meta-bar', 'product-list.product-facet__product-list' and 'product-item__image-wrapper' (Prestige-style theme markup). Each product must have a model image as its second image (the first being the product shot, or the reverse depending on the store's setup), because the toggle only swaps image order via CSS. No metafields or apps are required (ticket field: MF/N). The snippet uses fixed element IDs (ed-model-view-button-open/close), so it supports one instance per page. The JS runs on DOMContentLoaded and the Shopify design-mode section load event; it does not re-bind after AJAX filtering or pagination, so this should be tested.

items: Toggle usage rate (share of sessions that use the toggle)
Conversion rate and revenue per session for collection-page visitors

images.caption: Checkbox layout: 'Tragebilder' toggle on the right of the meta bar, next to the product count ('21 Produkte').
Icon-based layout: shirt icon (product, active with underline) and person icon (model) – reference design for the classic variant.
Button layout: 'Model | Produkt' text buttons with underline on the active option, shown next to 'Filter & Sortieren'.

Theme editor: 'Model view' block on the collection template with Position, Layout, Checkbox/Button/Classic settings and tooltip options; the classic layout is shown live ('Opinion:' + shirt/person icons, centered).
